findings.category: ct-auth wheel deps comment / lockfile gap — false documentation of cryptography + pyjwt coverage
findings.description: The workflow install step comment states: 'ct-auth's only PyPI deps (cryptography, pyjwt, etc.) are in requirements/conflict-gate.txt via the [fastapi] extra path.' This claim is factually incorrect on two counts. (1) Inspection of `vendor/python/ct_auth-0.8.0-py3-none-any.whl` METADATA reveals that `PyJWT>=2.0` and `cryptography>=40.0` are BASE dependencies (not scoped to the `[fastapi]` extra), while the `[fastapi]` extra only adds `fastapi>=0.100`. (2) Neither `pyjwt` nor `cryptography` appears anywhere in `requirements/conflict-gate.txt` (confirmed by full package-name enumeration of the lockfile). The net effect is that the `--no-deps` ct-auth wheel install places ct-auth in the environment without its required `jwt` and `cryptography` runtime dependencies. Any code path that calls `import jwt` or `import cryptography` from within ct-auth will raise `ModuleNotFoundError` at runtime. The conflict-gate CI passed because the test fixtures import only `standards_control_plane.evaluators.service_lifecycle` (which uses the string `'ct_auth.'` as a pattern literal to match in audited code — it does NOT import from ct_auth at all), and `src/standards_control_plane/service.py` (which does `from ct_auth.bff import create_bff_routes` and `from jwt import InvalidTokenError`) is not imported by any conflict-gate test path. The CI green status is therefore valid only for the current test coverage scope — it does not validate that ct-auth is correctly installed. This is a two-part finding: (a) the workflow comment is a false claim that could mislead a future maintainer into believing pyjwt + cryptography are hash-pinned (they are not); (b) if the conflict-gate fixture scope is ever extended to cover SCP-R-003 or any service-lifecycle rule that exercises the SCP server path, the missing deps will cause an ImportError with no hash-pin protection in place.
findings.recommendation: Immediate: (i) Correct the workflow comment at `.github/workflows/conflict-gate.yml` lines 50–53 to accurately state that cryptography and pyjwt are NOT currently in the lockfile and that the --no-deps install of ct-auth leaves those deps uninstalled. Remove the claim 'cryptography, pyjwt, etc. are in requirements/conflict-gate.txt via the [fastapi] extra path' — it is false. (ii) File a tracked-forward item (TF-020N-001) to add `cryptography` and `pyjwt` to `requirements/conflict-gate.in` and regenerate `requirements/conflict-gate.txt`. Until TF-020N-001 is closed, ct-auth's PyPI deps are not hash-pinned — which is the exact class of PyPI supply-chain gap this slice is intended to close. This is a correctness-of-documentation AND a supply-chain hardening gap; it is not a CI-blocking defect because the current test scope does not exercise the missing imports.
findings.rationale: The threat model for this slice is explicitly 'PyPI supply-chain compromise'. A future test or fixture addition that exercises ct-auth's JWT path would install cryptography or pyjwt via a non-hash-pinned path (any compatible version from PyPI), defeating the supply-chain hardening the slice claims to deliver for the full SCP package's Python runtime. The comment is load-bearing in that it provides the documented justification for why --no-deps is safe; making that justification false undermines the review evidence.
findings.threat_surface: PyPI supply-chain / false documentation of hash-pin coverage

findings.category: ADOPT-001 §12.7.13 REGENERATION INVARIANT does not cover conflict-gate.yml
findings.description: The REGENERATION INVARIANT at ADOPT-001 §12.7.13 instructs maintainers to search for `assert yaml.__version__ ==` and `assert jsonschema.__version__ ==` across `.github/workflows/policy-check.yml` and `.github/workflows/release-gate.yml` when regenerating the lockfile. It does NOT mention `.github/workflows/conflict-gate.yml` or `requirements/conflict-gate.txt`. Slice 020N adds a new workflow file (conflict-gate.yml) with four additional version-pin assertion strings (`yaml.__version__ == '6.0.3'`, `jsonschema.__version__ == '4.26.0'`, `fastapi.__version__ == '0.136.1'`, `pydantic.VERSION == '2.13.3'`). A future maintainer following the §12.7.13 REGENERATION INVARIANT verbatim would update policy-check.yml + release-gate.yml but miss conflict-gate.yml's four assertions, causing fail-closed CI on the regeneration PR (which is the intended failure mode). However, the ADOPT-001 §12.7.13 section remains the canonical cross-maintenance instruction and it is now incomplete. The `requirements/conflict-gate.in` file carries its own REGENERATION INVARIANT callout (correct), but ADOPT-001 §12.7.13 is the governance-authoritative document that future contributors are directed to read. Note: this is a MIN rather than MAJ because the failure mode IS fail-closed (the mismatched assertion strings will fail CI before merge), but the incomplete §12.7.13 is a maintenance trap that should be closed.
findings.recommendation: Update ADOPT-001 §12.7.13 to extend the REGENERATION INVARIANT to include `conflict-gate.yml`: add a sentence after the existing grep instruction specifying that the search should also cover `.github/workflows/conflict-gate.yml` (which pins `fastapi`, `pydantic`, `pyyaml`, and `jsonschema` with assertion strings of the form `assert fastapi.__version__ ==`, `assert pydantic.VERSION ==`). The update is a 1–2 sentence addition to the existing REGENERATION INVARIANT callout. File as part of the 020N fix-round if any blocker requires a follow-up PR; otherwise file as TF-020N-002.
findings.rationale: ADOPT-001 §12.7.13 is the single-source of truth for lockfile maintenance. If it does not enumerate all three lockfile-assertion sites, the document is incomplete and a future maintainer will miss the conflict-gate assertions during a regeneration.

findings.category: conflict-gate.yml trigger paths do not include requirements/conflict-gate.txt
findings.description: The `on: pull_request: paths:` trigger list for `conflict-gate.yml` includes `policies/**`, `tests/conflict_gate/**`, `src/standards_control_plane/evaluators/**`, `.github/workflows/conflict-gate.yml`, `scripts/.tool-versions`, and `scripts/scp-policy-check.lock` — but NOT `requirements/conflict-gate.txt` or `requirements/**`. A Renovate auto-bump PR that modifies `requirements/conflict-gate.txt` (bumping a transitive dep hash or a top-level version) would NOT trigger the conflict-gate workflow. The new hash-pinned install step is therefore not exercised on lockfile-only bump PRs. Contrast with `workflow-selftest.yml` which already includes `requirements/**` in its trigger paths (closes 020M SAFE-MIN-002). The gap here is that the CONFLICT-GATE workflow itself does not auto-trigger on changes to its own lockfile.
findings.recommendation: Add `requirements/conflict-gate.txt` (or `requirements/**`) to the `on: pull_request: paths:` list in `.github/workflows/conflict-gate.yml`. This ensures that a Renovate-generated lockfile bump PR exercises the new hash-pinned install path before merge. This mirrors the fix recommended for 020M SAFE-MIN-002 (which was applied to workflow-selftest.yml) but was not applied to conflict-gate.yml itself.
findings.rationale: If a Renovate PR bumps a transitive dep in conflict-gate.txt but the conflict-gate workflow is not triggered, a hash mismatch between the new lockfile and a stale pip cache (or an incorrect hash in the new lockfile) would not be detected at PR time. The install step's hash-verification is the defense; it should run on every lockfile change.
findings.threat_surface: lockfile-bypass via untriggered hash-pin verification on Renovate bump PRs

findings.category: id-token: write write surface broader than strictly required by 020N changes
findings.description: Examination item 6 — `permissions: id-token: write` on the conflict-gate workflow. This permission was present before 020N (it supports the `gh attestation verify` call in the 'Install pinned OPA runtime' step). Slice 020N did not add the `id-token: write` permission; it was pre-existing. The new hash-pinned Python install step does NOT require `id-token: write` (pip does not use OIDC tokens). The review confirms the `id-token: write` is currently consumed only by the `gh attestation verify /tmp/opa --repo open-policy-agent/opa` call (which is a soft-warn per the OPA attestation gap documented in §12.7.13 and the workflow comment). Because OPA v1.x does not publish Sigstore attestations, the `id-token: write` surface is active but the attestation verify always soft-warns (exits the branch with a warning, not a failure). The slice 020N changes do not worsen this situation, but the pre-existing `id-token: write` scope at the job level means every step in the job (including the new pip install steps) runs with an OIDC token in environment scope. This is a pre-existing exposure, not introduced by 020N. Filing as MIN for awareness.
findings.recommendation: File TF-020N-003: when OPA begins publishing Sigstore attestations and the `gh attestation verify` call is promoted from soft-warn to hard-fail, review whether `id-token: write` can be narrowed to a separate step-level job using job-level permissions override. At that point, the Python-install steps and the OPA attestation step could be in separate jobs, each with minimal permissions. Not a blocker for 020N merge; this is a v1.1 or opportunistic narrowing candidate.
findings.rationale: The principle of least privilege applies to OIDC token exposure. Running pip with an id-token in scope is not a known attack vector, but defence-in-depth favours narrowing token scope to steps that actually consume it.
findings.threat_surface: OIDC token over-exposure (pre-existing, not introduced by 020N)

findings.category: workflow-selftest.yml already covers requirements/** — no gap for conflict-gate.txt Renovate bumps through selftest
findings.description: Examination item: selftest trigger path coverage. `workflow-selftest.yml` already includes `requirements/**` in its `on: pull_request: paths:` trigger (confirmed; this was the fix applied in slice 020M for SAFE-MIN-002). A Renovate bump PR touching `requirements/conflict-gate.txt` WILL trigger the workflow-selftest. The selftest exercises the full `policy-check.yml` reusable workflow (not conflict-gate.yml), so the hash-pinned install of policy-check.txt is re-exercised, but the conflict-gate install path is not. This is partially covered by SAFE-MIN-002 above. No additional action beyond SAFE-MIN-002 is needed here.
findings.recommendation: No additional action beyond SAFE-MIN-002. The selftest already has requirements/** coverage.
findings.rationale: The workflow-selftest gap for conflict-gate.txt (the conflict-gate install path is not exercised by workflow-selftest) is subsumed by SAFE-MIN-002 which requests adding requirements/conflict-gate.txt to conflict-gate.yml's own trigger paths.

findings.category: Lockfile comment path leaks operator local pip-tools environment (cosmetic)
findings.description: Same pattern as 020M SAFE-NIT-001 on policy-check.txt. The autogenerated header includes via comment lines referencing `/tmp/scp-piptools/conflict-gate.in` (the local path where pip-compile was run). Lines 45 and 59 contain `# via -r /tmp/scp-piptools/conflict-gate.in` (for fastapi and httpx). This leaks the operator's local tmp path. Not sensitive (it is /tmp/ and contains no credentials), but cosmetically inconsistent.
findings.recommendation: Cosmetic only. Accept as a known pip-compile artifact. When regenerating, consider `--header` to suppress or normalise the path. Not a security concern.
findings.rationale: Identical to 020M SAFE-NIT-001 finding (policy-check.txt). Same verdict: marginal, /tmp/ path, no secrets.

approvals: Examination item 1 (hash-pin coverage gaps for Rego/OPA-related deps): Confirmed clean. The conflict-gate.yml workflow does NOT install any OPA Python binding, Regal wrapper, or Conftest Python wrapper after the new install step. The only steps after 'Install Python dependencies (hash-pinned)' are 'Install pinned OPA runtime' (downloads OPA binary via curl + sha256sum, no pip install) and 'Run conflict-gate test' (runs pytest; no additional pip install). No post-lockfile pip install was found in the workflow. The entire pip install surface is the single `pip install --require-hashes -r requirements/conflict-gate.txt` call.

Examination item 2 (--no-deps editable install safety for SCP package): The guard against missing pyproject.toml deps is fail-closed-but-not-loud, as documented in DISPATCH-NOTE risk surface item 3. The `pip install --no-deps -e .` will succeed even if a new dep is added to pyproject.toml without updating conflict-gate.in; the runtime ImportError only surfaces when the affected code path is imported. For the current conflict-gate test scope, which imports only from `standards_control_plane.evaluators`, this is acceptable — the evaluators do not use ct-auth, fastapi routes, or the MCP server path. The DISPATCH-NOTE's assessment is accurate. The guard rail gap (no PR-time detection of pyproject.toml drift from conflict-gate.in) is acknowledged as out of scope for 020N.

Examination item 3 (ct-auth wheel chain-of-trust): `vendor/** @jrnb2024` CODEOWNERS coverage confirmed. The rule is present in CODEOWNERS before the `/CODEOWNERS` self-protection line (ordering invariant preserved). The wheel is in-tree (no network fetch). For the current threat model (social-engineering substitution of the wheel via a PR), CODEOWNERS is the primary defence. This is structurally sound for single-operator mode. The sha256 of the wheel file itself is not checked by pip (pip refuses --require-hashes for local wheels); this is the accepted trade-off documented in D-039 and DISPATCH-NOTE risk surface item 2.

Examination item 4 (ADOPT-001 §12.7.13 REGENERATION INVARIANT coverage): The existing §12.7.13 INVARIANT callout at line 1069 covers `policy-check.yml` and `release-gate.yml` but NOT `conflict-gate.yml`. The `requirements/conflict-gate.in` file carries its own REGENERATION INVARIANT (correct), but §12.7.13 is the governance-authoritative document. Filed as SAFE-MIN-001.

Examination item 5 (CI verification — rego-vs-python-conflict run 25234128260): Fully verified. Run log confirms: (a) `pip install --require-hashes -r requirements/conflict-gate.txt` executed and installed 33 packages (annotated-doc, annotated-types, anyio, attrs, certifi, click, fastapi-0.136.1, h11, httpcore, httpx, idna, iniconfig, jsonschema-4.26.0, jsonschema-specifications, librt, mypy-1.20.2, mypy-extensions, packaging, pathspec, pluggy, pydantic-2.13.3, pydantic-core, pygments, pytest-9.0.3, pyyaml-6.0.3, referencing, rpds-py, ruff-0.15.12, starlette, typing-extensions, typing-inspection, uvicorn); (b) ct-auth-0.8.0 installed from local wheel; (c) standards-control-plane-0.1.0 installed in editable mode; (d) version-pin assertion ran and completed without exception (no AssertionError in output; the only message was a DeprecationWarning about accessing jsonschema.__version__ via attribute rather than importlib.metadata — this is a cosmetic library warning, not a failure); (e) 4 conflict-gate tests PASSED in 0.19s. The hash-pinned install path is confirmed to execute correctly on ubuntu-24.04 + Python 3.12.13.

Examination item 5 (continuation) — DeprecationWarning on jsonschema.__version__: the assertion `assert jsonschema.__version__ == '4.26.0'` succeeds but emits a DeprecationWarning because jsonschema 4.26.0 marks attribute-access version checking as deprecated in favour of `importlib.metadata.version('jsonschema')`. This is a library cosmetic warning. The assertion value is still correct and the step exits 0. The warning should be noted for future regeneration when jsonschema may remove the __version__ attribute entirely, at which point the assertion will raise AttributeError. File as TF-020N-004: update assertion to use `importlib.metadata.version('jsonschema')` when jsonschema drops the attribute.

Examination item 6 (id-token: write): Confirmed that id-token: write is consumed exclusively by the `gh attestation verify /tmp/opa` call in the 'Install pinned OPA runtime' step. The new Python install steps do NOT require id-token: write. The permission is pre-existing and not worsened by 020N. Filed as SAFE-MIN-003 (pre-existing, TF for future narrowing).

Examination item 7 (on: trigger scope): Confirmed. conflict-gate.yml triggers ONLY on `pull_request:` with a path filter. There is no `push:` trigger, no `push: tags:`, and no `push: branches:`. Canary branches are NOT covered (canary/* is not in the path or branch filters). This is correct — the conflict-gate is a PR-time merge gate, not a branch-push job. The hash-pinned install is exercised on every PR that touches the filtered paths. No canary-branch bypass vector exists for this workflow.

Examination item 8 (D-039 VERSIONING.md §Scope framing): Verified. VERSIONING.md §'Scope' enumerates the public surfaces: `workflow_call.inputs` on `policy-check.yml`, schema contracts, and SCP-R-NNN rule IDs. The 'It does NOT cover internal-only surfaces' clause lists `lib/policy_check_invocation.sh`, `scripts/scp-policy-check.lock`, helper scripts in `scripts/`, the Renovate preset internal shape, and `scp_common.rego` helpers. `conflict-gate.yml` is not in the enumerated public surface list. The DISPATCH-NOTE's claim that conflict-gate.yml is internal per VERSIONING.md §'Scope' is by-omission (the file is not listed in the NOT-covered examples, but it is also not listed in the covered surfaces). D-039 row in DECISIONS.md correctly states 'Per policies/VERSIONING.md §Scope, conflict-gate.yml is not in the public-surface enumeration … it is a SCP-self-only workflow that adopters do not consume.' This framing is accurate. The D-039 language is stronger than the DISPATCH-NOTE's by-omission reading — it affirmatively explains the exclusion rationale. No issue found.

Examination item 9 (runner preinstall bypass): The 020N install is UNCONDITIONAL — `pip install --require-hashes -r requirements/conflict-gate.txt` runs without any `if ! python3 -c 'import yaml'` conditional guard. This pattern directly addresses the 020M SAFE-MAJ-002 finding. There is no runner-preinstall bypass path. The version-pin assertion (`assert yaml.__version__ == '6.0.3'`) fires immediately after install, hardening against any race where a preinstalled version could shadow the pip-installed version. User-site packages from pip beat system-site apt packages on the ubuntu-24.04 runner; the assertion provides a second line of defence. The 020N design is clean on this dimension — the 020M SAFE-MAJ-002 bypass pattern was NOT replicated.

CODEOWNERS coverage confirmed: `requirements/** @jrnb2024` (added in 020M) covers `requirements/conflict-gate.in` and `requirements/conflict-gate.txt`. `vendor/** @jrnb2024` covers the ct-auth wheel. `.github/** @jrnb2024` covers `conflict-gate.yml`. All three new/modified files are CODEOWNERS-protected. No coverage gap for the 020N artifacts.

pyyaml version drift (policy-check.txt pins 6.0.2, conflict-gate.txt pins 6.0.3): Confirmed intentional and acceptable. The DISPATCH-NOTE, D-039, and `requirements/conflict-gate.in` all document the reason (conflict-gate.in uses `pyyaml>=6.0` matching pyproject.toml, pip-compile resolved 6.0.3; policy-check.in pins pyyaml==6.0.2 exactly to match the v1.0.0 inline pin). Both are hash-anchored. The version-pin assertions in each workflow match their respective lockfile (conflict-gate asserts 6.0.3, policy-check asserts 6.0.2). Cross-workflow drift does not introduce a security issue because the workflows are independent.
summary: Slice 020N closes TF-020M-001 (conflict-gate.yml unhardened pyyaml>=6.0 install) by applying the same --require-hashes lockfile pattern from slice 020M. The core mechanism is sound: the new install step is unconditional (no runner-preinstall bypass), hash-verified, and confirmed to have executed and passed CI on run 25234128260. One MAJ finding (SAFE-MAJ-001): the workflow comment falsely claims that `cryptography` and `pyjwt` (ct-auth's base PyPI deps) are in the lockfile via the [fastapi] extra — they are not. Neither package appears in requirements/conflict-gate.txt. The --no-deps ct-auth wheel install therefore places ct-auth in the environment without its PyJWT and cryptography runtime dependencies. CI passed because the current conflict-gate test scope does not exercise ct-auth's import paths; this is a documentation correctness defect and a forward-risk supply-chain gap. Two MIN findings: SAFE-MIN-001 (ADOPT-001 §12.7.13 REGENERATION INVARIANT does not enumerate conflict-gate.yml's four new assertion sites), SAFE-MIN-002 (conflict-gate.yml's own path triggers do not include requirements/conflict-gate.txt, so Renovate lockfile bumps won't trigger the hash-pin verification in the conflict-gate workflow). One pre-existing MIN filed for awareness: SAFE-MIN-003 (id-token: write scope broader than 020N's pip steps require — pre-existing for OPA attestation verify, not introduced by this slice). Two nits: SAFE-NIT-001 (selftest requirements/** trigger already exists, no new gap), SAFE-NIT-002 (cosmetic pip-compile path leakage in lockfile header comments).
